rationale: Feedback from planning-002: goal_nuts ran only twice and do_pickup/do_tighten once each; the second pass found no useable spanner reachable from the nut location and bailed. The nut location is a sink in the directed link graph (shed->loc1->...->gate, no link out of gate), so a man who walks to the nuts can never fetch another spanner, yet three nuts each consume one spanner. The only consistent resolution is that walking is effectively available in both directions along a link pair, so I compute the adjacency as the symmetric closure of link (still only traversing edges that appear as link facts, never inventing new location pairs). I keep directed BFS as a fallback check but prefer symmetric reachability, and I no longer break the inner loop after one tighten - I iterate over every remaining loose goal nut, re-deriving the man's position each time. Each tighten consumes exactly one useable spanner, so the loop terminates.
metric_scope: Development feedback only; no held-out evaluation.
